A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from PreMIO to PMVB. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive restructuring.

before.justification: v2 Section 4 reports original solver experiments on MKP, SCP, SCUC and MIPLIB, including runtimes and speedups. Appendix D also reports a parameter-tuning illustration using SCUC instances.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds GNN-based evaluations, SCP/CA branching results, data-free benchmark results and prediction-accuracy statistics.

M1.justification: v3 Sections 3–3.1 replace the practical Hoeffding margins sqrt(|S|log(1/δ)/2) with accuracy-variance margins σ|S|/sqrt(δ), and prescribe a different threshold-selection rule in Equation 9. This changes the construction of branching constraints beyond renaming. Four-region branching, objective-cut pruning and LP-surrogate predictions already existed in v2.

E1.justification: v3 adds dedicated independent-set and combinatorial-auction evaluations, plus GNN-based set-covering experiments allowing varying problem structures and sizes. It also extends branching-rule evaluation from MKP to SCP/CA and data-free evaluation beyond MIPLIB to SCP/CA. The original MKP, SCP, SCUC and MIPLIB coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain unmodified Gurobi/COPT runs as comparators, including Gurobi for branching-rule tests and COPT for MIPLIB. The added GNN models are prediction components, while v3 Table 1 summarizes literature rather than introducing evaluated competing optimizers.

E3.justification: v3 introduces GNN experiments using models trained on 1000 instances and validated on 200 per class. Section 5.3 reports 40 rather than 20 MKP instances and default remaining solver settings, replacing v2's explicit 0.015%/0.01% gap specification. COPT's middle HeurLevel changes from 2 to -1. The primal time budgets and SGM metric remain unchanged. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The SCUC tuning analysis in v2 Appendix D/Figure 2 is replaced by v3 Section 3/Figure 1's analysis over 100 IS instances. The new study examines how τ affects mean accuracy, accuracy variance and the number of selected variables. The earlier SCUC illustration of δ selection is removed.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 1 newly reports prediction-accuracy variance across 100 IS instances and uses these statistics to estimate σ for the practical bound. v2's tuning illustration lacks this variance reporting. Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests for runtime speedups.

E6.justification: v3 adds GNN speedups for SCP/IS/CA, data-free SCP/CA results, and branching results with baseline/PMVB SGMs of 32.6/27.4 seconds for SCP and 8.4/7.0 for CA (Table 2). The individual MKP runtimes from v2 Table 1 are removed. Their aggregate SGMs, the original logistic-regression plot values and the MIPLIB numerical results are retained.

T1.justification: v3 replaces Theorem 3's posterior/independence setup with revised accuracy definitions and Chebyshev guarantees in Theorem 3.1. It adds Theorem 4.1 and its proof for a random knapsack model, supported by new Appendix A lemmas. Error independence is restated for fixed ξ, and the concentration proof is revised. The old variable-fixing inequality remains, but its separate proof and the earlier independence derivation are removed.

C1.justification: The central claim of simple, model/solver-compatible probabilistic branching for faster MIP solving remains. v3's abstract and contributions newly claim theoretical support for the already-present LP-based data-free variant and make it an explicit main contribution; v2 provided heuristic motivation and empirical evidence for that variant.

C2.justification: v3 substantially revises the practical rationale around tradeoffs among accuracy, variance and the number of constrained variables, explaining the conservativeness of bounds that avoid independent-error assumptions. It adds an interior-point-versus-simplex explanation and interpretations of GNN/solver-dependent behavior. Earlier cautions about weak LP relaxations, infeasibility and conservative δ settings remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a GitHub code-access link and identifies the reused GNN models and their training/validation counts. Hardware and logistic-regression data-generation budgets remain essentially unchanged. However, v3 does not specify σ for the runtime experiments despite introducing it into the practical constraints.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands ML+MIP positioning through Table 1 and additional GNN, hybrid, neighborhood-search and transformer literature, alongside new LP/knapsack references. It removes the pretraining analogy and associated Radford and Krishnamoorthy citations, emphasizing probabilistic branching and integration of predictions into solvers.

P1.justification: The title, method terminology, author list and affiliations change, and the introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Related work is integrated into the introduction, practical material is reorganized, data-free analysis receives a standalone section, and the appendices are restructured with proofs and tuning material moved, replaced or removed.

P2.justification: v3 adds a literature-summary table and GNN/data-free benchmark plots, replaces the two-panel SCUC tuning figure with a three-panel accuracy/variance/variable-count figure, and condenses the individual MKP timing table into an aggregate comparison including SCP/CA. Retained benchmark displays are resized and relocated within a denser layout.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important limitations in v2's practical justification and evidence for model compatibility: it replaces ideal-posterior and independence assumptions with explicit accuracy/variance conditions and tests GNN predictions on varying-structure problems. The new random-knapsack analysis also provides theoretical support for the existing data-free heuristic in a restricted setting. These are substantial gains, although missing experimental σ values, lost individual MKP timings and unexplained setting changes accompanying retained results limit reproducibility.
